payload.reasoningSummary: Two of four usable fixture finance answers confuse NPV sign or time boundary, while one carbon answer confuses capture and avoidance and one record needs no change. A focused text-explanation follow-up could change the first-improvement priority. This is a simulated judgment; no real Round 2 is authorized.

plan.interpretation: Resolve the observed simulated finance-explanation obstacle before selecting one first improvement, while preserving the competing carbon-definition concern. This follow-up plan was written after inspecting validated Round 1 values.
plan.participants: Continue only the labeled offline fixture demonstration. A future real follow-up would require suitable consenting participants, fresh distribution approval and clear reporting of repeat exposure/learning effects.

uncertainties.rationale: Two fixture explanations confuse annual expense or savings with negative discounted project value.
A carbon-boundary concern and a no-change response compete with the proposed finance explanation.

questions.prompt: Consider this proposed explanation, not a tested UI: 'The illustrative model's NPV is -134.6 million constant 2025 USD: discounted net cash flow over the modeled period. A negative value means discounted costs exceed benefits under these assumptions; it is not an annual expense or a saving.' How would you explain the financial trade-off now, and what remains unclear?
questions.rationale: Probe the specific sign/time-boundary misunderstandings observed in two Round 1 fixture answers. If the explanation remains unusable, a different first change may be needed. Prompted comprehension cannot prove UI effectiveness.

questions.prompt: After that explanation, what one change, if any, would most help you explain the overall results, and why? Another change or no change is acceptable.
questions.rationale: Allow the observed carbon-boundary concern and no-change view to challenge an NPV-first choice rather than force agreement.

plan.analysisCriteria: Validate actual fixture answers for this new round. Assess whether each explanation distinguishes discounted project value from annual expense/savings; preserve residual carbon concerns and disagreement. Compare only within this simulated exercise and report prompting/learning limits. Stop at two rounds.
